title: Southern Hemisphere gyre AOU changes on sigma0 26.0-26.8 (GLODAP 1985-2023) do not follow the North Pacific winter-surface density rule; pre-set sign and size tests fail
abstract: Question: earlier work linked the North Pacific (NP) oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 to a lighter late-winter surface where the class outcrops, with a shift rule (AOU profile moves by 0.40-0.70 of the surface lightening) and an outcrop-area rule. Do the South Pacific (SP), South Indian (SI) and South Atlantic (SA) subtropical gyres follow these rules out of sample? Approach: GLODAPv2.2023 bottle AOU interpolated to sigma0 classes 25.6-27.2 in 15-40 degree boxes; cell-matched changes between 1985-1997, 2003-2012 and 2013-2023 with a cruise bootstrap; WOA23 decadal late-winter surface density in 25-55 degree formation bands; a pre-registered plan with three tests. Results: the same code gives the known NP gain (1985-1997 to 2013-2023: observed +12.1 umol/kg, 90% CI +9.0 to +13.8; shift rule +10.0 to +15.3). In the SH the pre-set sign test passed in 1 of 6 cases and the size test in 0 of 6, mainly because WOA23 SH surface changes give predictions below 1 umol/kg; the class-pattern test passed (5 of 6). Before 2005 only 3-13% of SH formation-band cells have late-winter salinity data (NP 58-69%), so those surface changes are not measured. Post hoc, ERSSTv5 shows thermal lightening of the SP (-0.053 kg/m3) and SA (-0.036) bands from 1985-94 to 2005-14, but SP AOU on 26.4-26.6 did not rise (-0.5 and -2.1 against +2.2 to +3.5 predicted) and fell by 1-5 on 26.4-26.9, while lighter SP classes 25.6-26.2 rose as predicted. SI AOU rose by +5.8 (+0.8 to +9.8) with no surface lightening. Pooled over 7 basin-intervals with observed surfaces, observed and predicted correlate (r = 0.78, permutation p = 0.02, slope 0.56), but this depends on the NH-SH contrast. Interpretation: the surface-density rule is an NP result with a large forcing signal, not a general law for subtropical thermocline AOU; SH changes need flow or wind-driven subduction terms. Limitations: no pre-2005 SH surface salinity; 5-13 cruises per SH basin and epoch; AOU with full preformed saturation; no spice decomposition; post hoc analyses are marked.

display.caption: Observed AOU change on sigma0 26.4-26.6 (GLODAP, cell-matched, 90% cruise bootstrap) against the NP shift-rule prediction from the late-winter surface change, for five basins and two intervals. Open symbols: late-winter surface unobserved in one decade (<40% of cells). a: pre-registered surface decades; b: no-lead decades with the post hoc fit to observed-surface cases.

a-b: WOA23 late-winter surface sigma0 change with the 26.5 outcrop (dots: no salinity data in one decade). c: fraction of 26.5 formation-band cells with late-winter salinity data per decade; SH bands are mostly unobserved before 2005. d: WOA23 total surface change in the 26.5 band and ERSSTv5 thermal part.
Observed AOU change (colour; 90% band for 1985-1997 to 2013-2023) and shift-rule prediction (black) for classes 26.0-26.8 in each basin, no-lead surface decades. Solid: E1-E3; dotted: E2-E3.
